issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Lecture is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement UML lists attributes in this order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors (problem_statement.md lines 63-68) and explicitly instructs students to create a constructor that follows the UML order (problem_statement.md lines 19-21). The reference solution, however, declares the constructor as: Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13), placing lectureName first. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected parameter order and may cause disagreements between student implementations, examples, and automated checks/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent across all artifacts. Two options: (A) Change the reference solution constructor signature to match the UML/instructions (for example: Lecture(int numberOfInscribedStudents, String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfTutors)), update the implementation accordingly, and adapt the template; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to explicitly list the constructor parameter order used in the solution (lectureName first). After choosing one option, update any example code and tests to use the same order so students are not confused.
